about.bio_1: Since a kid, I've always been interested in technology and building things. I started writing code at 13, turned it into a real job at 15, and never stopped. From RPA scripts to full platforms, the challenges just keep growing.
about.bio_2: Today I'm a full-stack developer, a Robotics Engineering student at UFV, and part of NERo, where I work on robot development. I like creating things, developing, and automating tasks.
about.quote: "Any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic." - Arthur C. Clarke

tagbot.title: TagBot
tagbot.description: An affordable educational robot that turns a phone into a controller and lets students explore programming hands-on.
tagbot.n_intro: A hands-on entry point to robotics: TagBot lets students control a real robot with a phone and see how code turns into motion.
tagbot.n_resultado_body: We built and tested a working prototype with an Android app and six control modes. NERo presented it with Brazil's Federal Revenue Service and at UFV's Semana do Fazendeiro. Classroom use is a planned next step, not yet deployed.
tagbot.n_contexto_body: Robotics often reaches schools through kits that are expensive or hard to adapt. TagBot aims to make a first experience more accessible with familiar components and a phone interface.
tagbot.n_construido_body:
The app lets students drive with buttons or a joystick, steer by tilting the phone, and program paths, timing, and motor speed. They can start with simple commands and advance to control concepts.

I implemented modular C++ firmware on the ESP32 and the Flutter app. Communication uses Bluetooth Low Energy and Wi-Fi; the app shows connection status and robot telemetry.
tagbot.n_hardware_body: The prototype integrates a USB camera, ultrasonic obstacle sensor, line sensor, and wheel encoders. These components support future lessons in perception and navigation.
tagbot.role: Technical software lead; ESP32 firmware and Flutter control app.
image_captions: Presentation with Brazil's Federal Revenue Service

asimav.title: AsiMAV
asimav.description: An autonomous drone for indoor missions. As AsiMAV's captain, I work on flight control, localization, and navigation for the Flying Robots League.
asimav.n_intro: At NERo/UFV, we are preparing a Parrot Bebop 2 to carry out indoor missions without GPS or a pilot. We have already taken an initial autonomous sequence from simulation to the physical drone.
asimav.n_resultado_body: We demonstrated an initial mission sequence with the physical drone, including takeoff, movement toward a landing platform, and return. This let us test autonomous execution beyond the simulator. Our next task is to make flight more precise and repeatable for the CBR 2026 challenges.
asimav.n_contexto_body:
The Flying Robots League at the Brazilian Robotics Competition challenges drones to identify landing platforms, navigate between targets, land precisely, and respond to human gestures. These missions take place indoors, where GPS cannot provide position.

As captain, I coordinate the team's work and contribute directly to software architecture, flight control, localization, navigation, and testing with the Bebop 2.
asimav.n_construido_body:
We connected the physical drone to a Gazebo simulation environment. Shared control interfaces let us develop algorithms in simulation before testing them on the Bebop 2.

We built odometry components that estimate relative position from velocity and orientation measurements taken by the drone's onboard sensors. A virtual map displays the traveled path, planned trajectories, and landing locations. Computer vision modules detect landing platforms and support mission execution.

We also developed an experimental gesture control system. It interprets arm movements and turns them into directional drone commands.
asimav.n_localizacao_body:
Without GPS, small position errors accumulate in flight. Our preliminary measurements suggest a potential error of about 5 cm per meter traveled, which makes longer routes less reliable.

We designed a strategy that uses landing platforms recognized by the camera as references to correct the position estimate. We are also exploring visual triangulation when two platforms are visible at once. Current work focuses on trajectory controllers, visual detection, and the drone's inertia, including during gesture control.
asimav.n_hardware_body: The Parrot Bebop 2 is our physical test platform. Gazebo reproduces the flight environment so we can develop and compare algorithms before each real-world test.
asimav.role: Team captain. I coordinate development and work on software, control, localization, and flight testing.

fluxo.title: Fluxo
fluxo.description: A live dashboard that helps restaurants spot queues, delays, and capacity limits before guests feel the impact.
fluxo.n_intro: Fluxo turns events on the restaurant floor into clear decisions for staff: where guests are waiting, which table needs attention, and when service is nearing its limit.
fluxo.n_resultado_body: The working prototype placed 3rd at Hackathon Abrasel, organized by TecnoPARQ in Viçosa from August 21 to 23, 2026. The team demonstrated the service cycle, operations panel, and live recommendations.
fluxo.n_contexto_body: During major events, demand at Viçosa restaurants changes quickly. Without measuring what happens on the floor, it is hard to know if a queue is growing, service will slip, or staff needs to be reassigned. We built Fluxo to give that view to businesses using ordinary phones and tablets.
fluxo.n_construido_body:
Staff record a guest's arrival, table, order, and delivery in a few taps. The system combines these events in a shared dashboard, measures waits, and flags situations needing attention.

In the FastAPI backend, the engine calculates arrival and service rates from live events, smoothed with EWMA, and uses queueing theory, including Erlang C, to project overload. A snapshot with estimates and recommendations is sent over WebSocket to the dashboard, table tablet, and staff phones.
fluxo.n_hardware_body: We laser-cut a tablet stand for the guest view, with a button to call a waiter. The staff panel runs in a browser on regular phones, with no dedicated hardware.
fluxo.role: Product development and operational decision logic during the hackathon, with the team.
image_captions: Fluxo team receiving 3rd place at Hackathon Abrasel

neroSite.title: NERo Website
neroSite.description: Institutional website in development to present NERo's projects, teams, and research clearly to a broader audience.
neroSite.role: Full-stack development of the lab's web presence with Vue and FastAPI.
neroSite.n_intro: The lab's work should make sense outside the lab, too. NERo's site is being built to show who works on robotics at UFV and what each team makes.
neroSite.n_resultado_body: The site is in development. It aims to bring projects, teams, and lab information into a clear experience for prospective students, partners, and visitors.
neroSite.n_contexto_body: Robotics projects combine software, electronics, and research, which can be hard to explain on a page. The site needs to provide context before technical detail and stay organized as the lab evolves.
neroSite.n_construido_body: I work on the Vue interface and the FastAPI service layer. The focus is a content structure that is easy to update, with clear pages for the lab and its projects. Features and publishing are still in progress.

robosPlatform.title: Robótica // Hub
robosPlatform.description: One place for UFV Robotics Engineering students to explore the curriculum, find study materials, and track exams and deadlines.
robosPlatform.n_intro: I built Robótica // Hub to turn scattered course information into a useful starting point for the class.
robosPlatform.n_resultado_body: The platform is live. Its graph shows all 55 courses and their dependencies; the archive organizes study materials by term and subject; the calendar tracks exams, assignments, and class events.
robosPlatform.n_contexto_body: Previously, the curriculum, materials, and dates lived in PDFs, message groups, and loose folders. It was hard to see what to study next, find an old problem set, or check a deadline. This is a personal initiative and does not officially represent NERo or UFV.
robosPlatform.n_construido_body:
I built a Vue 3 application with a curriculum graph navigable by zoom, search, and minimap. The archive syncs from a shared Google Drive folder; uploads send multiple files directly to Drive with server-side authorization.

The calendar reads a sheet maintained by the class, so new dates appear without code changes. I handled the design, architecture, implementation, and publishing.
robosPlatform.role: Independent initiative: design, architecture, development, and publishing.

terrasafe.title: TerraSafe
terrasafe.description: A low-cost sensor prototype that tracks conditions on slopes and sends alerts to a live map.
terrasafe.n_intro: Rain is only part of the story: TerraSafe was created to measure how the soil on a slope responds to it.
terrasafe.n_resultado_body: The prototype won 1st place at SmartCamp Cidades Inteligentes in June 2026. At the event, one to three sensors demonstrated the full path from reading to alert.
terrasafe.n_contexto_body: A rain forecast alone does not show how much water a slope has already absorbed. Local measurements can add context for people monitoring risk areas. TerraSafe explores an affordable network of measurement points for that purpose; it is still a prototype, not a deployed warning system.
terrasafe.n_construido_body:
Each unit measures soil moisture, tilt, air temperature, and humidity. Data travel between sensors over ESP-NOW, reach a local hub, and go to a FastAPI backend that updates a map and flags readings above configured thresholds.

The architecture avoids requiring Wi-Fi at every measurement point. The prototype uses an ESP32, capacitive moisture sensor, DHT11, MPU6050, and 18650 battery.
terrasafe.n_hardware_body: A unit combines ESP32, environmental sensors, and a rechargeable battery in a probe designed for partial burial. Estimated prototype cost was R$60 to R$80 per unit.
terrasafe.n_escala_body: A municipal pilot and larger network still depend on field validation, sensor calibration, and partnerships with responsible agencies. For now, the results demonstrate the technical flow at small scale.
terrasafe.role: Sensor prototype and visualization platform development with the team.

r2d2.title: R2D2: autonomous AI robot
r2d2.description: An R2-D2-inspired robot planned to combine conversation, computer vision, and autonomous navigation. I lead 15 students from concept to physical prototype.
r2d2.role: Leading 15 students: software architecture, technical roadmap, task distribution, mentoring, and system integration.
r2d2.n_intro: We are developing a robot intended to perceive its surroundings, recognize people, converse, and move without a pilot. The work spans mechanical design through onboard intelligence.
r2d2.n_resultado_body: R2D2 is in development. The team is planning the architecture, organizing modules, and building software and hardware foundations. A fully integrated physical prototype is the long-term goal; the capabilities below are still being developed or planned.
r2d2.n_contexto_body:
The Star Wars character inspires R2D2's appearance. We are designing a functional robot that can navigate and interact autonomously. The work brings mechanical design, electronics, perception, AI, and navigation into one platform.

I coordinate a multidisciplinary team of 15 students at NERo/UFV. I set technical milestones, assign tasks, review implementations, and make sure independently developed parts can work together.
r2d2.n_construido_body:
The body and mechanisms will be modeled in CAD, including motors, sensors, and internal component placement. Before deploying algorithms to physical hardware, we plan to model the robot with ROS 2, URDF, RViz, and Gazebo to test motion, sensors, and behavior in simulation.

A modular design lets the team develop mechanics, control, perception, and interaction in parallel, with clear interfaces between them.
r2d2.n_interacao_body:
We plan to combine speech recognition, voice synthesis, and language models so the robot can understand commands and converse in context. Cameras and other sensors should support recognition of people and objects.

Model selection and deployment on the target hardware still need testing. The aim is for these capabilities to help the robot interpret its surroundings and choose appropriate actions.
r2d2.n_navegacao_body: To move around indoors, the robot will need to localize itself, map spaces, and plan routes without constant human control. The team is exploring ROS 2, LiDAR, depth cameras, SLAM, obstacle avoidance, and path planning. These capabilities will be validated in simulation before physical integration.
r2d2.n_plataformas_body:
Capybot explores human-robot interaction: face recognition, speech, and AI conversation. Sentinel-X studies mobile robotics: sensors, mapping, and navigation. Their lessons and modules are intended to support R2D2's intelligence, perception, and mobility.

The planned architecture includes technologies such as Python, C++, OpenCV, Whisper, Piper TTS, Raspberry Pi, and ESP32. Final choices depend on testing and integration across the team.
